target.title: fix(codex): dedupe replayed side-question tool calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can replay the same pending `item/tool/call` request when a client connection is rebound. The main attempt path already reuses an in-flight execution by `threadId`, `turnId`, and `callId`, but the `/btw` side-question path did not. A replay there could execute a non-idempotent OpenClaw tool twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the existing Codex dynamic-tool execution registry in the side-question path.
- Treat `callId` as the protocol request identity: the same `threadId` / `turnId` / `callId` replay shares one execution promise.
- Keep requests with different `callId` values independent, even when their tool names and arguments match.
- Remove the earlier payload-equivalence coalescer, which could suppress a legitimate distinct tool call and misattribute its timeout, diagnostics, or observer callbacks.
- Extend the existing side-question bridge regression test to cover both same-ID replay and distinct-ID execution.

## User Impact

A replayed side-question tool request no longer repeats its external side effect, while intentional calls with distinct Codex call IDs continue to run independently.

## Evidence

- Final PR surface against current `main`: 2 files, +50/-15.
- Upstream Codex contract checked at `openai/codex@0fb559f0f6e2`:
  - `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs` defines `call_id` on `DynamicToolCallParams`.
  - `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs` registers pending dynamic-tool responses by `call_id`.
  - `codex-rs/app-server/src/outgoing_message.rs` replays the original pending request when rebinding a connection.
- Regression behavior: two concurrent requests with the same `callId` plus one request with a different `callId` produce three successful protocol responses and exactly two underlying tool executions (`tool-1`, `tool-2`).
- Focused three-file Vitest run: 96/96 passed.
- Final side-question Vitest run: 56/56 passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.88).
- What was not tested: no live Codex connection-rebind E2E was run. Full local tsgo was not usable because the shared dependency tree was stale after merging current `main`; the observed errors were in unrelated packages and no touched Codex file produced an error. The new-head PR CI is the canonical broad proof.

Validation commands:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output`
- `git diff --check upstream/main`

## Linked Context

Related issue: #80040
